result.title: Dependency Graphs of Mathematical Arguments: Representation, Structural Measurement, and Proof Review
result.summary: We propose a source-grounded framework for representing and measuring mathematical arguments with assistance from large language models. It includes numbered and unnumbered statements, equations, assumptions, and constructions, distinguishing source occurrences from contextual states and inference records. Proposed dependencies retain source evidence and review status. A measurement contract fixes manuscript versions, boundaries, granularity, proof choices, and macro anchors. On a selected finite directed acyclic graph, depth is the longest prerequisite-path length, and bulk counts distinct ancestor edges. We give a union recurrence that accounts for shared subarguments and identify reachability conditions preserving depth and the macro skeleton; unrestricted refinement need not preserve depth or bulk. A standardized, versioned prompt protocol separates annotation discovery, deterministic recomputation, and review assistance. Cross-paper links support a research agenda on theorem co-use, rare combinations, and connections between dependency communities. These patterns motivate probabilistic premise suggestions and review of possible omissions or unchecked application conditions in human-written and AI-generated proofs. Further applications include source-linked reading support and comparison of individual and collaborative argument shapes. We provide an evaluation design rather than empirical evidence of these benefits. Suggested premises require mathematical validation, and the measures describe a specified representation rather than intrinsic mathematical difficulty, originality, or importance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一个由 LLM 辅助、来源可追溯的数学论证依赖图表示与测量框架：区分原文语句、假设与推理记录，定义深度和 bulk 等结构度量，并设计版本化的标注与复核提示协议及评测方案，但未提供实证结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用依赖图刻画推理步骤、以深度度量前提链长度，并把证据来源与复核状态附着于依赖上，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的结构化表示、计算深度评价和前提遗漏审查提供概念线索，能否迁移尚待核查。
